brief.greeting: Good morning. Kernel Rust finally stopped poking holes in its own code, and GNOME gave us a calm desktop night.

stories.headline: Safe self‑referential structs land in kernel
stories.body: **No more unsafe gymnastics:** Gary Guo showed a Rust pattern that lets the Nova driver hold self‑referential data without unsafe blocks. The demo ran at Kangrejos 2026 and could replace most C tricks.
stories.why: If you write drivers, you can drop a lot of manual pointer juggling.

stories.headline: 2.8 trillion tokens power new language model
stories.body: **Scale meets open data:** A Hugging Face blog details an open pipeline that crunched 2.8 trillion Indic tokens, pushing pre‑training limits for low‑resource languages.
stories.why: More data means better models for languages you actually speak.

stories.headline: GNOME OS Preview offers stable desktop base
stories.body: **Less nightly, more steady:** LWN reports GNOME OS Preview ships a stable‑based edition built from GNOME 51.1, giving users a calmer alternative to the bleeding‑edge Nightly.
stories.why: You get a reliable desktop without chasing every upstream change.

quick_hits.text: **Podcast:** Hackaday Episode 391 covers ESP32 SDR, vintage pager hacks, and a Mars rover bug report.
**Security:** LWN notes a batch of Linux distro updates patched dozens of packages on Friday.
**Badge:** Hackaday warns first‑time event badge designers about power‑budget and solder‑bridge pitfalls.
**Repo:** DownpourRecomp v1.0 unlocks 60 FPS and DualSense triggers for Silent Hill: Downpour on Windows.
**Model:** LiquidAI LFM2.5‑24B‑A2 downloaded 9,356 times on Hugging Face.

brief.sign_off: That’s your two‑minute tech sprint. Keep coding, and enjoy the ride .

highlights.title: [$] Safe self-referential data structures in kernel Rust
highlights.summary: Gary Guo presented a kernel Rust solution for safe self‑referential data structures at Kangrejos 2026, potentially eliminating most unsafe code in the Nova driver.
highlights.detail: The approach leverages the pin_init crate to create immovable structures without unsafe code, offering a path to safer Rust components in the Linux kernel.

highlights.title: Hackaday Podcast Episode 391: Tuned in to ESP32 SDR, New Old Pagers, and Bugs on Mars
highlights.summary: Hackaday Podcast Episode 391 covers an ESP32 SDR project, vintage pager hacks, and a Mars rover bug report.
highlights.detail: Hosts Elliot Williams and Tom Nardi discuss the upcoming Philadelphia hacker conference and the phase‑out of the EZ80 microcontroller, linking these topics to the episode’s broader hardware hacking themes.

highlights.title: How Itaú is building generative AI for its entire customer base
highlights.summary: Itaú is deploying its ia.i conversational interface and IARA governance platform to deliver generative AI services to customers and employees in Brazil's regulated banking sector.
highlights.detail: The rollout follows the bank's AI First strategy, extending AI capabilities beyond internal tools to public-facing applications while adhering to strict financial regulations.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: LWN reports a batch of security updates released Friday for multiple Linux distributions, covering dozens of packages.
highlights.detail: The updates affect AlmaLinux, Debian, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, and SUSE, addressing vulnerabilities in components such as Ghostscript, Grafana, Wireshark, and the Linux kernel among others.

highlights.title: The Trials And Tribulations Of Your First Badge
highlights.summary: Hackaday explains common pitfalls when designing a first event badge, despite the simple hardware required.
highlights.detail: While assembling a microcontroller, buttons, battery, and display seems straightforward, the article highlights design, firmware, and production challenges that often surprise first‑time badge makers.

items.title: Introducing GNOME OS Preview
items.summary: GNOME OS Preview releases a stable‑based edition built from GNOME 51.1, offering a less volatile alternative to the Nightly build.
items.detail: The preview uses the same GitLab branches as the org.gnome.Platform Flatpak runtimes and is intended for non‑developer users, providing greater stability after a year of daily Nightly usage.

items.title: Results from the 2026 TAB election
items.summary: The 2026 Linux Foundation Technical Advisory Board election re‑elects four members and adds Laurent Pinchart as a new member.
items.detail: Incumbents Kees Cook, Dave Hansen, Miguel Ojeda, and Shuah Khan retained their seats, indicating continuity in the board’s technical direction.

items.title: LittleBitUA/DownpourRecomp
items.summary: DownpourRecomp v1.0 provides a native Windows port of Silent Hill: Downpour with 60 FPS unlocked and DualSense adaptive‑trigger support.
items.detail: The static recompilation of the Xbox 360 binary includes a warm‑cache ROV, a standalone launcher, and portable save handling, and has been tested on US and EU X360 dumps.
